title: Ratnamanjari and the Test of Generosity
summary: The first statue Ratnamanjari challenges King Bhoja and tells how Vikramaditya gave away his entire kingdom to a beggar without hesitation.
moral: True generosity expects nothing in return

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Ratnamanjari stops King Bhoja from ascending the throne

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She narrates how Vikramaditya gave his kingdom to a brahmin who asked for it

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja admits he cannot match such selfless generosity

title: Chitra Rekha and the Golden Mongoose
summary: The second statue tells of a golden mongoose who tested charity at a great yajna, and only Vikramaditya's kitchen passed the test.
moral: The value of charity lies in the sacrifice behind it

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Chitra Rekha challenges Bhoja's worthiness

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells of the mongoose who judged every offering until it found Vikram's — given during famine from his own last meal

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja reflects on whether his charity has ever truly cost him anything

title: Chandra Kala and the Honest Woodcutter
summary: Vikramaditya disguises himself as a common man and encounters a woodcutter who returns a bag of gold to its rightful owner despite his poverty.
moral: Honesty is the wealth of the poor and the duty of all

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Chandra Kala questions if Bhoja values honesty above all

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She narrates how Vikram witnessed and rewarded the woodcutter's integrity

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja acknowledges that rewarding honesty is itself a virtue

title: Kama Khandala and the Fearless King
summary: Vikramaditya walks alone into a den of dacoits to rescue a kidnapped child, armed only with his courage.
moral: Courage is not the absence of fear but action in spite of it

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Kama Khandala asks Bhoja if he has ever risked his life for a stranger

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram entered the bandits' cave alone and freed the child through sheer bravery

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja confesses that he has always sent soldiers rather than going himself

title: Leelavati and the Impartial Judge
summary: Vikramaditya must judge a case where his own son has committed a crime. He punishes his son as he would any citizen.
moral: Justice must be blind even to one's own blood

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Leelavati asks Bhoja if he can judge without favor

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram sentenced his own son to the same punishment as a commoner

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja sees that impartial justice demands superhuman detachment

title: Ravi Bhama and the Patient King
summary: A courtier insults Vikramaditya publicly. Instead of punishing him, the king listens, discovers a legitimate grievance, and corrects it.
moral: Patience and humility reveal the truth that anger would hide

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Ravi Bhama asks if Bhoja can bear insult with grace

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She narrates how Vikram turned a public humiliation into a moment of just reform

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja admits that his pride would have demanded punishment first

title: Kaumudi and the Keeper of Promises
summary: Vikramaditya promises a dying enemy safe passage for his family. Despite pressure from ministers, he honors the vow completely.
moral: A king's word is his bond, even to an enemy

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Kaumudi asks Bhoja if his promises are unbreakable

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram protected his dead enemy's family against his own advisors' wishes

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja realizes that a promise honored under pressure is the only promise that matters

title: Pushpavati and the Demon's Boon
summary: A demon offers Vikramaditya unlimited power in exchange for one innocent life. The king refuses and defeats the demon through wit.
moral: Power gained through injustice is poison disguised as nectar

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Pushpavati asks if Bhoja would refuse absolute power

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She narrates how Vikram outwitted the demon without sacrificing anyone

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja acknowledges the temptation of easy power and the strength needed to refuse it

title: Madanavati and the Compassionate Warrior
summary: After a great battle, Vikramaditya tends to wounded enemy soldiers with the same care as his own. His generals are outraged.
moral: Compassion for the defeated is the mark of a true victor

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Madanavati asks if Bhoja shows mercy to enemies

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram personally bandaged enemy soldiers and fed them from the royal stores

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja sees that war ends on the battlefield but humanity must never end

title: Vijaya Sundari and the Wise Arbitrator
summary: Two neighboring kingdoms are about to go to war over a river. Vikramaditya arrives and resolves the dispute so both kingdoms prosper.
moral: The wisest victory is one where no blood is shed

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Vijaya Sundari asks if Bhoja seeks peace before war

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She narrates how Vikram proposed a canal system that shared water equally

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja learns that creative solutions prevent more suffering than any army

title: Sundarvati and the Disguised King
summary: Vikramaditya disguises himself as a peasant to learn the true condition of his people, and is humbled by what he discovers.
moral: A king who does not know his people's suffering is no king at all

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Sundarvati asks Bhoja when he last walked among common folk

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram lived as a farmer for a week and reformed corrupt tax collectors

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja is shamed into realizing he rules from a distance

title: Trilochana and the Truthful King
summary: A rival king offers peace if Vikramaditya will tell a single lie. Vikram refuses and wins the war through truth alone.
moral: Truth is the most powerful weapon a just ruler possesses

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Trilochana asks if Bhoja has ever compromised truth for convenience

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She narrates how Vikram's absolute truthfulness earned the loyalty of even his enemy's soldiers

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja understands that credibility is built over a lifetime and lost in a moment

title: Padmini and the Selfless Protector
summary: During a plague, Vikramaditya stays in the city nursing the sick while his court flees. He nearly dies but saves thousands.
moral: A leader who abandons his people in crisis is no leader

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Padmini asks Bhoja if he would stay when danger comes

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram organized medicine, burned infected cloth, and held dying hands

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja realizes leadership means being the last to leave, not the first

title: Kirtimati and the Learned King
summary: Vikramaditya settles a debate between scholars by demonstrating that true knowledge serves the people, not the ego.
moral: Knowledge that does not serve others is vanity

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Kirtimati asks if Bhoja values learning or the appearance of learning

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram silenced proud scholars by asking what their knowledge had done for the hungry

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja reflects on the difference between wisdom and mere scholarship

title: Sunanda and the Forgiving King
summary: An assassin sent to kill Vikramaditya is captured. Instead of execution, Vikram forgives him and gives him land to farm.
moral: Forgiveness can transform an enemy into a friend

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Sunanda asks if Bhoja could forgive someone who tried to kill him

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She narrates how the forgiven assassin became one of Vikram's most loyal subjects

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja admits he would have ordered execution without a second thought

title: Manohari and the Just Taxman
summary: Vikramaditya discovers his own tax minister has been exploiting the poor. He personally returns every coin and reforms the system.
moral: A ruler is responsible for the actions of those who serve in his name

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Manohari asks if Bhoja knows what his ministers do in his name

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram went village to village returning stolen taxes from his own treasury

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja sees that delegation without oversight is abdication of duty

title: Anuradha and the Humble King
summary: A child asks Vikramaditya a question he cannot answer. Instead of pretending, the king admits ignorance and asks the child to teach him.
moral: Humility to learn is the beginning of true wisdom

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Anuradha asks if Bhoja can admit when he is wrong

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram knelt before a shepherd boy to learn about the stars

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja recognizes that his courtiers never hear him say 'I don't know'

title: Dharmavati and the Night Patrol
summary: Vikramaditya patrols his city at night in disguise and rescues a woman being robbed, fighting the thieves himself.
moral: Duty does not sleep when the sun goes down

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Dharmavati asks what Bhoja does while his city sleeps

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She narrates how Vikram made nightly rounds ensuring every citizen was safe

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja understands that a king's duty is a full-time devotion, not a daytime occupation

title: Varunini and the Bridge Builder
summary: Vikramaditya labors alongside common workers to build a bridge after a flood, refusing to let his status excuse him from physical work.
moral: A leader who will not share his people's toil has no right to share their harvest

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: Statue Varunini asks if Bhoja has ever dirtied his hands for his people

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: She tells how Vikram carried stones alongside laborers for seven days

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja looks at his unblistered hands and understands the statue's point

title: Jaya Lakshmi and the Final Test
summary: The last statue tells King Bhoja that hearing all thirty-two tales and understanding them IS the test. Bhoja bows and walks away from the throne.
moral: The one who knows he is unworthy of power is the one most worthy of it

acts.name: challenge
acts.summary: The final statue asks Bhoja what he has learned from all the stories

acts.name: tale
acts.summary: Bhoja recounts each virtue — generosity, courage, justice, humility, compassion, truth, patience, forgiveness

acts.name: judgment
acts.summary: Bhoja chooses not to sit on the throne, proving himself worthy — the throne rises to heaven
